chunks: Divorce of the Sunnah is (where) he divorces her with a (valid) divorce, meaning upon the purity (from menstruation) without copulation, with the testimony of two witnesses. Then he leaves her until she completes her menstrual periods ('idda). So when her menstrual periods are gone, she is irrevocably separated from him, and he would be a suitor among the (other) suitors — if she wishes she may marry him, and if she wishes not, then (she need not). And if he intends to return to her (ruju'), he should call witnesses to his returning to her before her menstrual periods pass, so she will be with him upon the previous divorce.
He (the narrator) said: And Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: 'These are the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
"Divorce is (only permissible) twice, then retention in good fellowship or release with kindness"
The second divorce is the release with kindness.'

key_terms.أقراء: Menstrual periods / waiting periods (singular: qar'); used to determine the 'idda
key_terms.بانت: She has become ba'in (irrevocably separated); the divorce has fully taken effect
key_terms.تسريح بإحسان: Release with kindness — one of the two options after each revocable divorce (Quran 2:229)
key_terms.رجعة: Ruju' — the husband's right to revoke a revocable divorce during the 'idda period
key_terms.طلاق السنة: Divorce according to the Sunna — the legally proper, revocable form of divorce

ai.seo_question: What is the proper Sunna-compliant divorce procedure in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated via the authoritative chain through Muhammad ibn Muslim from Imam al-Baqir (AS), defines the canonical Sunna-compliant divorce procedure. Imam al-Baqir explains that a revocable (raj'i) divorce must occur during the wife's period of purity, without preceding intercourse, and must be witnessed. The husband may revoke (ruju') before the 'idda expires — but after 'idda, she becomes irrevocably separated (ba'in) and he would need a new marriage contract. A supplementary narration from Abu Baseer through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) anchors the second revocable divorce in Quran 2:229, equating the 'release with kindness' with the second divorce.
